evidence: TaskController.ts createTask: res.status(201).json({ id: task.id, projectId: task.projectId, title, description, status, dueDate: task.dueDate ? task.dueDate.toISOString() : null, assigneeId })
TaskController.ts assignTask: the same object literal is repeated inside res.json({...}), including the dueDate ISO/null conversion
TaskController.ts markTaskAsDone: the same object literal is repeated a third time
TaskController.ts listTasks: tasks.map((task) => ({ id, projectId, title, description, status, dueDate: task.dueDate ? task.dueDate.toISOString() : null, assigneeId })) is the fourth copy
ProjectController.ts createProject: res.status(201).json(project) sends the raw use-case result with no mapping, unlike TaskController
ProjectController.ts and TaskController.ts: every handler repeats catch (error) { const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error'; res.status(400).json({ error: message }); }
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both controllers do share one job: they are Express HTTP adapters that pass requests to use cases. The problem is that the response contract for a Task is written out four separate times. Each copy has the same seven fields and the same rule that `dueDate` becomes an ISO string or null. That rule should live in a single mapper or presenter. Error handling is also copied: the same `catch` block that turns any error into a 400 appears in every handler in both files. On top of that, the two controllers shape responses differently. ProjectController sends the raw result of the use case with `res.status(201).json(project)`. TaskController maps each entity to an explicit DTO first. So the module has no shared way to present responses. Together, the duplicated rule and the inconsistent approach fail the rubric.

violations.message: The Task response mapping, including the rule that dueDate becomes an ISO string or null, is written out four times (createTask, assignTask, markTaskAsDone, listTasks) instead of living in one mapper or presenter. Error-to-400 handling is also repeated in every handler.

createProject sends the raw use-case result with res.status(201).json(project). TaskController maps entities to explicit DTOs, so the module has no consistent way to present responses. It also repeats the same catch/400 error handling instead of sharing it.
